description: "The process of estimating how uncertain a model's predictions are."
term: "Uncertainty Estimation"
letter: "U"

difficulty: "Advanced"

## Simple explanation

Uncertainty estimation helps a system express when it is unsure about a
prediction. This can support decisions such as asking for human review,
collecting more data, or abstaining from an answer.

## Technical explanation

Uncertainty may reflect irreducible noise in observations (aleatoric
uncertainty) or limited knowledge of the model (epistemic uncertainty).
Methods include calibrated probabilities, ensembles, Bayesian approaches,
and predictive intervals. Estimates require validation under relevant
distribution shifts.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Confidence-aware systems can handle ambiguous inputs more responsibly and
prioritize review. A model's raw score is not necessarily a calibrated
uncertainty measure, especially on unfamiliar inputs.

## How it works

An estimation method produces a probability, interval, disagreement score,
or other uncertainty signal alongside predictions. The system evaluates
whether that signal matches observed errors, then defines thresholds or
fallbacks appropriate to the task's risk.

## Practical example

A document classifier can send cases with low calibrated confidence to a
human reviewer. Evaluate coverage and error rates at different abstention
thresholds, including on data that differs from the training distribution.

## Common misconceptions

- A model's maximum softmax score is not automatically a reliable
  uncertainty estimate.
- High confidence does not guarantee correctness, especially for
  out-of-distribution inputs.
